description:
Asks for the DNS records of the domain to be checked, once you have published them. The check
is asynchronous: the call returns `202` with the domain as it is now, usually still `PENDING`,
and its `status` changes to `VERIFIED` or `FAILED` when the check finishes. Read the domain with
`GET` to see the result. A domain that is not `VERIFIED` 72 hours after it was registered is
removed and its name is freed.

- **Add-on:** requires the custom email domain add-on, which is contracted with BeeL. Without
  it the call answers `403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
- **`EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_READY` (`409`):** the domain is still registering (`dns_records: []`); repeat
  the call in a few seconds.
- **Sending service failure:** if the check cannot be requested the call fails with `502` and nothing changes.
- **Unpaid billing:** when the billing of the account is unpaid the call answers `402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED`.
- **Credentials:** it requires a live API key or a dashboard session. A test API key answers
  `403 LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry does not repeat the operation.

BeeL API endpoint: POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/email-domains/{email_domain_id}/verify (reference: https://docs.beel.es)

account_id.description: Your own account, or an account you provisioned. The account in the path, not the credential, decides which account the operation acts on. A `403` is returned when you do not reach it, the same response an account that does not exist gets.

idempotency_key.description: Optional idempotency key for this operation. Omit it and one is derived from the request itself, which makes a blind retry safe but also collapses a SECOND, deliberately identical operation into the first for 24 hours. Set it — to an order id, or anything unique per intended operation — whenever you mean to create something that may look identical to what you just created.

name: beel_verify_email_domain
